ledger.title: A call writing through a second out formal does not poison a pointer out slot
ledger.text: Found by OUT-PARAMETER-SCALAR-FRAME-PREMISE: `int r(char **buf, size_t *size) { … *buf = data; memcpy(size, &n, sizeof n); return 0; }` validates its out slot (rules 11r(6) and W4 alike) with no premise, because a contracted call with `Borrowed` positions writes no binding, so nothing poisons `*buf` though `memcpy`'s character-typed copy may alias the caller's pointer object (fixture a_copy_into_the_second_formal_is_not_read_under_the_premise pins the current behaviour; the effective-type premise is never consulted for it). Pre-existing and wider than the premise: any `Borrowed` call actual pointing at writable memory. DISCHARGE: decide, with a census of the bodies that rely on it, whether a call taking a pointer to writable memory must poison the out slots it may reach (memcpy, memmove, memset and every borrowed-pointer callee), and implement that refusal with fixtures and Lean parity, or record the reading as a stated premise.
